text:
priya: Heads up — saw a 25% p99 tail regression on mistral-7b staging after yesterday's batching heuristic tweak. Appears when sequences slide past max_pos boundary (we use 4096) and we hit wraparound. logs attached below. :frowning:
jack: oof, can you paste the profiling slice? is kernel chooser switching to fallback kernels?
priya: pasted sample from trace: 
```
# profile snippet
kernel_selector: chosen=fast_matmul_v2
seq_len=4100 batch=8
kv_cache_size=4096 -> wrap_detected
fallback_path_taken: true
latency_ms: 220 -> 285
```
jack: fast_matmul_v2 should be fine but fallback_path_taken=true is suspicious. maybe we mis-handle pos index > max_pos and end up copying KV segments repeatedly.
miguel: I remember a corner case — when RoPE scaling + sliding window overlap crosses max_pos we rewrite the position indices and the KV-tile alignment moves, which can force a suboptimal kernel that expects aligned tile boundaries.
elaine: can you repro with a minimal script? I want to run microbench on a single GPU and dump kernel selection traces.
priya: repro script (quick):
```
# minimal repro
from runtime import Client
c = Client(model="mistral-7b", max_pos=4096)
prompt = "A\n" * 4105  # forces sliding window + wrap
resp = c.generate(prompt, stream=False)
# set env RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_select,kv_debug
```
priya: run above on staging and you should see fallback path and burst of memcpy on KV resize.
jack: thanks. hypothesis: our batching heuristic merged two requests where one had pos near 4090 and other small; when we continuous-batch we ended up with merged kv pointer that crossed boundary and triggered a "resize+shift" logic that is O(n) and changes kernel tag.
miguel: agree. fix options: 1) update batching heuristic to avoid combining requests if (a.current_pos + incoming_len) > max_pos - safety_margin, 2) make the KV shift path use an in-place rotation that preserves tile alignment, or 3) allow kernel selector to prefer tile-agnostic kernel in those cases (costly).
elaine: prefer (1) as quick mitigation, then (2) long-term. can we add a unit test where two batches with pos 4090 + 20 get split?
priya: i ran quick experiment: disabling cross-boundary coalescing drops p99 back to baseline. cheap toggle: BATCHER_AVOID_WRAP=true
runtime-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for commit abc123 to staging (batcher-wrap-fix) :rocket:
jack: nice — but watch throughput delta. Avoiding coalescing will reduce batching efficiency on long sequences. we should add a heuristic: only avoid coalescing if estimated kv-copy-cost > batching-savings. need cost model.
miguel: i sketched numbers in thread: kv-copy ~ O(kv_len) ~ 4k tokens -> ~3 ms per request on gpu for our memcpy pattern, while batching gain for 8 -> ~20% throughput improvement (~10 ms saved). so for single wrap event it's still worth batching unless it causes fallback kernel with +60ms tail.
elaine: can we add a cheap check in the batcher: if predicted_kernel_tag_after_merge != predicted_kernel_tag_before_merge then don't merge. we already have kernel-tag heuristic for mem-managed kernels, maybe reuse.
priya: good idea. kernel_tag predictor exists but wasn't invoked in cross-batch merge. i've opened a small PR to call it. patch: 
```
# pseudo
before_tag = predict_kernel_tag(batch_state)
after_tag = predict_kernel_tag(batch_state + incoming)
if before_tag != after_tag:
    push_to_next_batch(incoming)
else:
    merge()
```

jack: please also log a metric for "kernel_tag_mismatch_batched" so we can quantify frequency.
miguel: also check RoPE scaling path — when we upscale RoPE for long-context we resample positions which can change parity of tile alignment. tiny bug: our pos_rescale used float rounding that sometimes yields off-by-one on boundary. that explains nondeterministic fallback.
priya: added pos_rescale fix to my branch and unit test that exercises pos index 4095..4105. tests pass locally.
elaine: run perf harness overnight on 7b and 8x7b, include both scaling on and off. schedule: start canary tonight, monitor p99, kernel-switch counters, and kv-memcpy bytes.
priya: ACK. i'll also add telemetry for max_position_embeddings hits (counter when seq_pos >= configured_max).
jack: one more ask — add a small synthetic that forces misaligned tiles and asserts kernel_selector returns same tag after KV-shift-algo change. helps avoid regressions.
miguel: agree. i'll own kernel-selector test.
priya: thanks team. will post follow-up tomorrow with canary numbers. :thumbsup:
